strategy_title: Fixing Transposed B-Matrix Load Index Yields No Improvement
strategy_description: Correcting the B-matrix load index from a column-major address (idx_m + 384*idx_n) to the intended row-major address (idx_m*1 + idx_n*384) produced virtually no change in any profiling metric: duration dropped by only 0.3% (200.32us → 199.71us), registers per thread remained at 255, occupancy stayed at 12.5% theoretical / ~10.6% achieved, shared memory bank conflicts remained at 8-way on ~70% of wavefronts, and MIO stalls remained at ~49% of cycles. This indicates the two index expressions are mathematically equivalent for this kernel's access pattern, or the Inductor-generated double broadcast_to wrapper was already computing the correct addresses despite its unusual form. When all key metrics are unchanged after a load-index fix, the original code was not actually buggy — the apparent 'transposition' was either intentional or already resolved by the compiler.
slow_pseudocode:
# BEFORE: apparent transposed load
idx_m = b_k_idx_vals          # [BLOCK_K, 1]
idx_n = offs_b_n[None, :]    # [1, BLOCK_N]
xindex = idx_n + 1536*idx_m  # shape [BLOCK_K, BLOCK_N]
b = tl.load(B + (tl.broadcast_to(idx_m + 384*idx_n, [BLOCK_K, BLOCK_N])).broadcast_to(xindex.shape))
# registers=255, duration=200.32us, bank conflicts 8-way 69.73%
fast_pseudocode:
# AFTER: 'corrected' row-major load
idx_m = b_k_idx_vals          # [BLOCK_K, 1]
idx_n = offs_b_n[None, :]    # [1, BLOCK_N]
xindex = idx_m * 1 + idx_n * 384  # [BLOCK_K, BLOCK_N]
b = tl.load(B + xindex)
# registers=255, duration=199.71us, bank conflicts 8-way 69.73% -- NO CHANGE
applicable_when: Never: this specific index rewrite produced no measurable improvement.
do_not_apply_when: When the before and after index expressions are mathematically equivalent for the actual tensor strides in use, or when the compiler's broadcast_to wrapper already resolves to the same memory addresses. Do not attempt to 'fix' Inductor-generated load indices based on visual inspection alone without verifying that the addresses actually differ at runtime. When registers_per_thread=255 and block limits are already at 2 blocks/SM, index-only changes cannot improve occupancy or bank conflicts.
framework_notes: In Triton/Inductor-generated kernels, the double tl.broadcast_to(...).broadcast_to(...) pattern may look like a transposed access but can resolve to the same addresses as the 'corrected' form due to how broadcasting interacts with the underlying pointer arithmetic. Always verify address equivalence before treating such patterns as bugs.
